messages.content: is my brother buys a book right?
yes. it can tell what he does, or be part of a story about him.
now use i.
i buy a book.
make it yesterday.
i bought a book yesterday.
now make it about him yesterday.
he bought a book yesterday.
ask if he did it.
did he buy a book yesterday?
why buy after did?
did goes with buy in that question. bought works without did in he bought a book yesterday.
only give the brother sentence again.
my brother buys a book.
write a longer story using lead about a person who knows a town well but asks where the group wants to go before choosing the way.

a woman knows the town well and can lead her family through it. before they leave the house, she asks what each person wants from the walk. her husband wants to buy bread, her sister wants to see the library, and the child wants to sit in the park. she looks at the places on a map and says they can do those things in that order without going back along the same road. knowing the town has helped, but it has not told her what the group wants. she needs their answers before choosing the way. when somebody asks why they are going to the shop first, she gives the reason from the plan. the group can follow her without knowing every road in town.
what does she ask before choosing where the group will go?
what each person wants from the walk.
what does her husband want?
to buy bread.
make the important idea of the story more simple.
she asks what the group wants before choosing where to go.
why is knowing the town not enough?
she still needs to know what they want to do there.
make that answer shorter.
knowing the town does not give their goal.
finish with them sitting in the park.
after the shop and library, they find a place in the park and sit together before going home.
use draws about my sister.
my sister draws a picture.
now make it yesterday.
my sister drew a picture yesterday.
use i instead for what i usually do.
i draw a picture.
now ask if she drew it.
did my sister draw the picture?
can you use drawing about now?
my sister is drawing a picture now.
why draw after did?
did goes with draw in that question. drew works without did in the sentence about yesterday.
only give the first sentence again.
my sister draws a picture.
i have four fruits on a plate. can you know they all taste the same?
no. different fruits can have a different taste.
make that answer shorter.
no. the group word does not give one taste for all.
now i say two taste good to me and two do not.
then two have a taste you like, and two have a taste you do not like.
can you know which fruits my sister likes?
no. your taste does not give her choice.
only tell me whether you know her choice.
i do not know which fruits your sister likes.
if she likes all four, is my answer wrong?
no. you can have different feelings about the same food.
only give how many fruits there are.
four fruits.
give me a sentence with eats about my father.
my father eats breakfast at home.
now make it yesterday.
my father ate breakfast at home yesterday.
use we for what we do every day.
we eat breakfast at home.
now ask if he ate breakfast.
did my father eat breakfast?
why eat after did?
did goes with eat in that question. ate works without did in the sentence about yesterday.
can you know he ate bread?
no. breakfast gives the meal, not the specific food.
only give the first father sentence again.
my father eats breakfast at home.
write a longer story about a child using the word vegetable but learning that this general word does not tell every detail needed for a meal. do not name specific vegetables.

a child helps his mother carry food into the kitchen. he puts two different vegetables on the table and says they are the same because both are vegetables. his mother asks whether he is talking about the same kind or only the same general group. he looks again and sees a difference in size, color, and how they feel in his hand. she says that a general word can help them talk about a group without making every object the same in every detail. when they look at the meal plan, they still need to know which vegetable is for which part. the child keeps the group word but also asks about the details needed for the task. he does not need a new word for every object to ask a useful question about it.
what did he get wrong about the general word?
he thought being in the same group made the two objects the same in every way.
what could he say instead?
these are both vegetables, but they are different objects with different details.
make the important idea of the story more simple.
a group word helps, but it does not tell every detail about each thing.
what question would help with the meal?
which vegetable do we need for this part of the meal?
finish with the two put in the right places.
he puts each vegetable where his mother asks, then looks at the list to see what they need next.
is he tries to read the sentence right?
yes. tries goes with he in that sentence.
now use they.
they try to read the sentence.
make it yesterday.
they tried to read the sentence yesterday.
ask if he tried too.
did he try to read the sentence too?
why try after did?
did goes with try in that question. tried works without did in he tried to read the sentence.
can you know he finished it?
no. trying does not always mean the task was finished.
only give the first he sentence again.
he tries to read the sentence.
my friend has a picture of a room. i have not seen it. i want to ask what is at the bottom without making up what is there.
what is at the bottom of the picture?
can i ask whether there is a chair?
yes, as a question: is there a chair at the bottom of the picture?
does that mean i know there is one?
no. the question leaves it open.
now my friend says there is a pan on the floor instead.
then you have the answer that a pan is at the bottom of the picture, on the floor of the room.
can you know what is in the pan?
no. you do not know what is inside from those details.
make that answer shorter.
no. the place does not give what is inside.
only give the first question again.
what is at the bottom of the picture?
use cleans about my brother and his room.
my brother cleans his room.
now make it yesterday.
my brother cleaned his room yesterday.
use we instead for something we do often.
we clean our room.
now ask if he did it.
did my brother clean his room?
why clean after did?
did goes with clean in that question. cleaned works without did when saying he cleaned his room.
can you know the room is still clean now?
not from yesterday alone. it may have changed later.
only give the first brother sentence again.
my brother cleans his room.
write a longer story about the word breaks. use something that breaks and also a person taking breaks, but keep the two ideas clear.

a child reads a story in which a small object breaks after a fall. later on the page, a person takes breaks while working. the child asks whether the same thing is happening in both lines. the teacher gives two short sentences to show the difference. one sentence is about an object no longer being whole. the other is about time away from a task. the child looks at the words around breaks and sees how takes changes the idea. he does not need to think that one word can have only one meaning. after the explanation, he writes his own two examples and asks whether each is clear. the word has stayed the same, but the work it does in the sentence is different.
what is the first breaks about?
an object that is no longer whole after a fall.
what is takes breaks about?
time away from a task while working.
make the important idea of the story more simple.
the same word can be about a broken object or about rest, with context making the difference clear.
give two simple examples.
the toy breaks. my father takes breaks while working.
finish with him using the rest meaning.
he writes that he takes breaks while reading, then puts the page with his book.
i had a cold drink with ice. i liked it, but i do not know what was in it.
you can say you liked the taste without knowing every part of how it was made.
can you know it was juice?
not as a fact. it could be juice, but cold and ice do not tell us what the drink was.
give me a question to ask the person who made it.
what did you put in this drink?
can i ask about sugar too?
yes. is there sugar in it is a clear question.
what if they say no?
then do not keep sugar as a fact. you can like the drink while learning that the reason for its taste was different.
only give the first question again.
what did you put in this drink?
can shall we read together be a question?
yes. it can give an idea and ask the other person to choose with you.
make that explanation shorter.
it asks whether the other person wants the idea too.
now make it about going for a walk.
shall we go for a walk?
can i answer no in a kind way?
yes. not now, thank you. i need some quiet time.
only give the no.
not now, thank you. i need some quiet time.
what if i only want to give a reason about time?
not now, thank you. i have to leave soon.
only give the reading question again.
shall we read together?
i drew three stars near a moon and two more near the top of the page. how many stars are in my drawing?
five stars.
explain that number.
three stars and two more make five.
yes, i added two. does that tell you how many stars are in the real sky?
no. it gives the number in your drawing, not the whole sky.
now i take one star out of the drawing.
then four stars are left in the picture.
can i still call it a night picture?
yes. your drawing can be about night without having every real star in it.
make that explanation shorter.
a picture does not need every star to be about night.
only give the number left in my drawing.
four stars.
the girl holds a book. does that tell us the book is hers?
no. holding a book does not always mean it is your own book.
now make it a past sentence.
the girl held a book.
ask whether she held it.
did the girl hold the book?
why hold after did?
did goes with hold in that question. held works without did in the girl held the book.
can you know she read it?
no. you gave holding, not reading.
only give the first holds sentence again.
the girl holds a book.
in my story, a child sees a plane. i want a question that gives a useful detail without making up where it is.
where is the plane when the child sees it?
now i say it is in a picture on the wall.
then the child sees a plane in a picture. the story does not say the child sees one outside.
make that answer shorter.
the plane is in a picture, not given as something seen outside.
can you ask what the child wants to know about it?
what does the child want to know about the plane in the picture?
why keep in the picture?
it keeps the question about the picture, rather than a real plane outside.
make that explanation shorter.
it keeps clear which plane you mean.
only give the first place question again.
where is the plane when the child sees it?
that question helped me get the detail right. please stop there.
okay. we can leave it there.
just a kind goodbye now.
goodbye, and take care.
now only goodbye.
goodbye.
